c.v: Facts given by the chip datasheet (sections 4.1.3.2 Reset and 4.1.3.3 Clock) in addition to the chapter text below:
If CPU Reset is from CPU0, the sensitive registers (the
PMS registers
in the chapter text below) will be reset, too.
Software reset is triggered by CPU
x
configuring its corresponding registers; see
Chapter 10
Low-power Management
for more details.
CPU clock: the application selects the clock source from the external main crystal clock, the internal fast RC oscillator (typically about
17.5 MHz
, adjustable) and the PLL clock.
The selected clock source drives the CPU clock directly, or after division, depending on the application.
Once the CPU is reset, the default clock source is the external main crystal clock divided by 2.
ESP32-S3 is unable to operate without an external main crystal clock.
RTC slow clock: used for the RTC counter, RTC watchdog and low-power controller.
It has three possible sources: external low-speed (
32 kHz
) crystal clock; internal slow RC oscillator (typically about
136 kHz
, adjustable); internal fast RC oscillator divided clock (derived from the internal fast RC oscillator divided by 256).
RTC fast clock: used for RTC peripherals and sensor controllers.
It has two possible sources: external main crystal clock divided by 2; internal fast RC oscillator (typically about
17.5 MHz
, adjustable).
